name: Narrator Talks
description: One cast member addresses the camera, lip-synced to the whole narration, with natural hand gestures. A chunky key-text sticker pops in on its key word while the character turns and points at it. The workhorse for hooks, intros and key statements.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

title.description: Key text shown on the sticker (2–8 words). Wrap one word in *asterisks* to highlight it.

kicker.description: Optional tiny label above the sticker (1–3 words).

keyword.description: Narration word on which the sticker pops (defaults to the most distinctive title word).

side.description: Which side the character stands on (landscape).

word.description: Narration word that triggers this acting beat (must appear in the narration).

pose.description: Body pose to snap into on the word.

mark.description: Emotion mark that pops over the head.

beats.description: Optional acting beats synced to words (0–4).

exampleNarration: Here's the first rule of money: save ten percent of every paycheck, before you spend anything. Make it automatic, and you won't even miss it.

name: Dialogue
description: Two cast members talk to each other with speech bubbles; each bubble's words light up as they are spoken and the speaker lip-syncs while the listener nods and reacts. Camera cuts shot/reverse-shot. The narration should contain the lines in order.

items.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

text.description: What they say — short, max ~12 words. Should match the narration wording.

endPose.description: Optional pose both take after the last line (e.g. celebrate).

lines.text: Wait, why is my code so slow?
You're loading the whole database on every click.
Oh. That's... a lot of data.
Add a cache and it'll fly!

exampleNarration: Wait, why is my code so slow? You're loading the whole database on every click. Oh. That's... a lot of data. Add a cache and it'll fly!

name: Walk and Talk
description: A character (optionally with a companion) strolls through a long scrolling world with parallax while talking; the camera tracks them. Optional speech-bubble lines alternate between walker and companion. Great for storytelling and transitions.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

items.description: Bubble line (max ~10 words), in narration order.

lines: Cities are getting hotter every summer.
Concrete soaks up heat all day.
exampleProps.caption: Urban heat

exampleNarration: Cities are getting hotter every summer. Concrete soaks up heat all day. So we need more trees!

name: Reaction
description: A character sets up a reveal, then reacts BIG when a number or fact slams in on its key word: snap pose, expression change, emotion mark, burst lines and a camera shake/push. Use for surprising stats and plot twists.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

text.description: The reveal — a number or 1–5 words (e.g. "$2.4 trillion").

prop.description: Optional icon next to the reveal.

word.description: Narration word on which the reveal lands.

setupPose.description: Pose before the reveal (e.g. think, talk).

exampleNarration: So I added up all the subscriptions I never use. The total? Fifteen hundred dollars a year. Gone.

name: Explain With Board
description: A character stands beside a whiteboard / screen / chalkboard and points at each item as it appears: a numbered list, a bar chart, a line chart, a big number or a big icon. Board style follows the location unless set.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

items.description: List item (max ~6 words); the item pops when its most distinctive word is spoken.

word.description: Narration word that triggers this acting beat (must appear in the narration).

pose.description: Body pose to snap into on the word.

mark.description: Emotion mark that pops over the head.

beats.description: Optional acting beats synced to words (0–4).

exampleNarration: Why does sleep matter so much? First, your memory gets saved overnight. Second, your muscles repair. And third, your mood resets for the next day.

name: Idea Moment
description: A character ponders a problem (thought bubble or question marks), then — on the key word — a lightbulb pops over their head, the camera snaps back and the idea lands as a sticker while they cheer. For solutions, insights and 'aha' beats.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

problem.description: Optional thought-bubble text before the idea (max ~8 words).

word.description: Narration word when the idea strikes.

kicker.description: Optional label above the idea sticker.

prop.description: Icon on the idea sticker (default lightbulb).

exampleNarration: I kept putting off every task, until I found a trick: the two minute rule. If it takes less than two minutes, do it right now.

name: Compare Two
description: Two characters each champion one option, with label stickers and a VS badge; each presents in turn while talking, then the verdict: the winner celebrates, the other shrugs (or both cheer on a tie).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).
Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

color.description: Optional stage colour (hex) when location is stage.

exampleNarration: Renting keeps you flexible with low upfront costs. Buying builds equity over time. In the long run, buying usually wins.

name: Establishing Shot
description: A sweeping camera move across a location with a big place/time tag; optional characters walk in from the sides and wave. Use to open a story, change location or start a chapter.

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

subcaption.description: Optional small label, e.g. a year or time of day.

items.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

exampleNarration: It's the summer of nineteen ninety nine, in the middle of Central Park.

name: Crowd Stat
description: A row (or two) of mini cast members hop in; on the key word the ones that make up the statistic light up and cheer while the rest fade — e.g. '1 in 4 people'. Big stat sticker on top.

word.description: Narration word on which they light up.

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

items.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

cast.description: Optional cast order to cycle through.

highlightColor.description: Optional hex colour for the highlight.

exampleNarration: Here's the scary part: one in four adults will face this at some point in their life.

name: Journey
description: A character walks (or runs) across a long scrolling landscape past signposts — one milestone per key word — and celebrates at the last one. For timelines, steps, processes and roadmaps.

character.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

word.description: Narration word when they reach it.

exampleNarration: You start with the basics. A few months later, you ship your first app. And a year in, you land your first job.

name: Title Card
description: Chapter / section opener: the cast hops onto a colourful stage and waves while a big title sticker slams in with a subtitle. Use at chapter starts.

items.description: Cast member (keep the same cast across the whole video).

location.description: Illustrated world. Keep locations consistent between neighbouring scenes.

exampleProps.title: The Money Mindset
exampleProps.subtitle: Why we spend the way we do

exampleNarration: Chapter two: the money mindset, and why we spend the way we do.
